n45442414735.s: The underlying principle of the Cabinet form of government in India is:
o: Supremacy of the President over Parliament
Collective responsibility of the Government to the people
Complete separation of the executive from the legislature
n45442414735.x: The Cabinet form is a mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people (UPSC 2017 key).

n3a8e1188a02.s: The expression 'ministers sink or swim together' means that:
o: Each minister answers only for his own department
All ministers must defend Cabinet decisions or resign
Ministers may publicly oppose Cabinet decisions
Only Cabinet Ministers share responsibility for policy
n3a8e1188a02.x: Collective responsibility requires all ministers to support Cabinet decisions publicly; a minister unwilling to defend such a decision must resign.

n33a3be6c9a5.s: The kitchen cabinet is criticised mainly because it:
o: Is a constitutional body with a fixed membership
Is directly answerable to the Lok Sabha
Is an extra-constitutional power centre that may bypass the Cabinet
n33a3be6c9a5.x: The kitchen cabinet is criticised as an extra-constitutional power centre because it may shape decisions while bypassing the formal Cabinet.

n105d43128a8.s: The death or resignation of the Prime Minister results in:
o: The Council of Ministers going out of office
Automatic dissolution of the Lok Sabha
The senior-most minister automatically becoming Prime Minister
Only the Prime Minister's office falling vacant
n105d43128a8.x: The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers, so his death or resignation means the Council of Ministers as a whole goes out of office.

n0f1ae9f0a24.s: Under Article 75(2), a Union Minister holds office during the pleasure of the:
n0f1ae9f0a24.x: Article 75(2) provides that a Union Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President; in practice the Prime Minister may ask a minister to resign or advise his dismissal.

ne024c502f6e.s: As of April 2025, how many Cabinet Committees function in India?
ne024c502f6e.x: There are eight: Appointments, Security, Political Affairs, Economic Affairs, Parliamentary Affairs, Accommodation, Investment and Growth, and Employment and Skill Development.

o: A Cabinet Committee formed under the Transaction of Business Rules
An informal inner circle of the Prime Minister's trusted colleagues and friends
The Cabinet Secretariat headed by the Cabinet Secretary
The Cabinet Ministers within the Council of Ministers
n6c0447a337b.x: A kitchen cabinet is an informal inner circle of the Prime Minister's trusted colleagues and friends, including some senior ministers and non-ministers.

nde7185555f6.s: During single-party majority eras, the dominance of the Union Cabinet over Parliament led to the criticism of a:
nde7185555f6.x: In single-party majority eras the Prime Minister and Cabinet generally dominated Parliament, leading to the criticism that the system resembled a 'cabinet dictatorship'.

n2395dd033cb.s: Cabinet Committees in India are formed under the:
n2395dd033cb.x: Cabinet Committees are extra-constitutional bodies formed under the Transaction of Business Rules, 1961, framed under Article 77(3).

n93bfd64371b.s: During 1989–2014, Cabinet cohesion and collective responsibility were weakened mainly by:
o: Direct exercise of Cabinet powers by the President
Coordination committees and demands of alliance partners
Frequent dissolution of the Rajya Sabha
n93bfd64371b.x: Coalition governments had to accommodate coordination committees and the demands of alliance partners, which weakened Cabinet cohesion and collective responsibility.

n2b284642d21.s: By convention, the Attorney General of India resigns when:
o: The Chief Justice of India retires
n2b284642d21.x: The Constitution fixes no term for the Attorney General, but by convention he resigns when the government changes.

nindian-polity-31-7.s:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:
1. He can speak in either House of Parliament.
2. He can vote on any motion or bill in Parliament.
3. He enjoys the privileges and immunities of an MP under Article 105(4).
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-polity-31-7.x: The Attorney General can speak in either House and enjoys MPs' privileges under Article 105(4), but he cannot vote, so statement 2 is wrong.

nindian-polity-31-8.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Advocate General of the State – Article 76
Solicitor General of India – Statutory post
Attorney General of India – Appointed by the Chief Justice of India
nindian-polity-31-8.x: The Solicitor General is a non-constitutional (statutory) post. The Attorney General is under Article 76 and appointed by the President; the Advocate General is under Article 165.

nindian-polity-31-13.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Attorney General of India?
o: He advises the Government of India on legal matters
He performs legal duties referred to him by the President
He holds office during the pleasure of the President
He performs legal duties referred to him by a State Governor
nindian-polity-31-13.x: The Attorney General performs legal duties referred by the President, not by a Governor; the State's legal adviser is the Advocate General.

nindian-polity-32-5.s:
Consider the following statements about the Advocate General under Article 177:
1. He can speak in the proceedings of both Houses of the State Legislature.
2. He can be named a member of a State Legislative Committee.
3. He can vote on any motion or bill in the State Legislature.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-polity-32-5.x: Under Article 177 the Advocate General can speak in both Houses and sit on committees, but he cannot vote, so statement 3 is wrong.

nindian-polity-62-4.s: Bicameralism was first introduced at the Centre in India by the:
nindian-polity-62-4.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 first brought bicameralism to the Centre (Council of State and Central Legislative Assembly); the 1935 Act brought it to some provinces.

nindian-polity-62-20.s: Which of the following can be abolished under Article 169 of the Constitution?
nindian-polity-62-20.x: A State Legislative Council, though a permanent House, can be abolished under Article 169; the Rajya Sabha cannot be abolished.

nindian-polity-9-16.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The President is an integral part of Parliament.
2. The Vice-President is not a part of Parliament.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-9-16.x: The President is an integral part of Parliament (Article 79), whereas the Vice-President, though Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, is not a part of Parliament.

n41c22714a80.s: 'If it agrees it is superfluous, if it dissents it is mischievous' — this criticism of a second chamber is attributed to:
n41c22714a80.x: This criticism of a second chamber is attributed to Abbé Sieyès.

n1f83229ad75.s: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar defended the Rajya Sabha mainly as a forum for:
o: Dignified debate and delaying hasty legislation
n1f83229ad75.x: Ayyangar regarded the Rajya Sabha as a forum for dignified debate that could delay legislation passed in the passion of the moment.

n4b4b4c632c1.s: For creating or abolishing a Legislative Council under Article 169, the State Assembly must pass a resolution by:
o: A simple majority of members present and voting
A two-thirds majority of the total membership
A majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
A majority of the total membership alone
n4b4b4c632c1.x: The resolution must be passed by a majority of the total membership and by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.

nindian-polity-62-37.s:
Which of the following States have bicameral legislatures?
1. Telangana
2. Bihar
3. Karnataka
nindian-polity-62-37.x: All three are bicameral. With Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh they make up the six bicameral States.

n75d07308797.s: The Legislative Council of Andhra Pradesh, abolished in 1985, was revived in:
n75d07308797.x: The AP Legislative Council was abolished in 1985 and revived in 2007; the 2020 resolution to abolish it again was withdrawn in 2021.

n6baa4f0559c.s: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years by the:
n6baa4f0559c.x: The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age under Article 326 from 21 to 18 years (in force 1989).

n18fbbfabd42.s: The Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution on Lok Sabha delimitation sought to freeze the Lok Sabha at:
n18fbbfabd42.x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly resolved to retain the Lok Sabha at 543 seats and preserve the approximate 2.2:1 Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio.

nindian-polity-12-5.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 81 – Duration of Houses of Parliament
Article 83 – Reservation of seats for SCs and STs
Article 330 – Composition of the Lok Sabha
Article 84 – Qualification for membership of Parliament
nindian-polity-12-5.x: Article 84 deals with qualifications for membership. Article 81 is composition, Article 83 duration and Article 330 SC/ST reservation.

nindian-polity-78-11.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The minimum age for membership of the Lok Sabha is 25 years.
2. The minimum age for membership of the Rajya Sabha is 25 years.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-78-11.x: The Lok Sabha's minimum age is 25 years, but the Rajya Sabha's is 30 years, so only statement 1 is correct.

nindian-polity-13-6.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha:
1. Among Union Territories, only Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir are represented in it.
2. Its quorum is one-tenth of its total membership.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-13-6.x: Both are true: only Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir among UTs are represented in the Rajya Sabha, and its quorum, like the Lok Sabha's, is one-tenth.

n12e0a386324.s: The gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot exceed:
n12e0a386324.x: Two sessions cannot be more than six months apart; this keeps legislative business going and the government accountable, though it fixes no minimum sitting days.

n31d9fdb7c27.s: Under Article 122, courts cannot inquire into parliamentary proceedings on the ground of:
n31d9fdb7c27.x: Article 122 bars courts from questioning parliamentary proceedings on the ground of alleged procedural irregularity.

nindian-polity-78-6.s: Which of the following minimum age requirements is NOT correct?
o: Prime Minister or Chief Minister – 25 years
nindian-polity-78-6.x: The Governor's minimum age is 35 years, not 30 (Article 157). The President and Vice-President need 35, and a PM or CM from the lower House 25.

nindian-polity-78-17.s: Which of the following pairs (office – minimum age) is correctly matched?
o: Prime Minister or Chief Minister – 25 years
nindian-polity-78-17.x: A Prime Minister or Chief Minister from the lower House needs 25 years. The correct ages are 21 for a municipal member, 30 for the Rajya Sabha and 35 for the Vice-President.

nindian-polity-78-34.s: The 61st Amendment, which lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years, came into effect in:
nindian-polity-78-34.x: The 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age to 18, and it took effect in 1989.

n6b6173da24c.s:
Assertion (A): The President is a component of the Parliament of India.
Reason (R): No Bill passed by both Houses of Parliament can become law without the President's assent.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n6b6173da24c.x: Both are true; the President's role in completing the legislative process is the reason for treating him as a component of Parliament under Article 79.

nd9dd2e18411.s: Before taking his seat, a Member of Parliament makes the oath or affirmation before:
o: The President or a person appointed by him
The Election Commission or a person authorised by it
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha only
nd9dd2e18411.x: Per the original's explanation, the oath or affirmation (Third Schedule form) is made before the Election Commission or a person authorised by it. (The original key wrongly marked the President.)

n5e47bf3ffe6.s: Under Article 103, a question of disqualification of an MP (other than under the Tenth Schedule) is decided by the:
o: Election Commission, after consulting the President
President, acting on the opinion of the Election Commission
Speaker or Chairman of the House concerned
Supreme Court, on a reference by the President
n5e47bf3ffe6.x: Under Article 103, the President decides the question after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission and acts according to that opinion.

n1efc963a45c.s: A vote against the party whip does not attract disqualification if the party condones it within:
n1efc963a45c.x: A vote or abstention contrary to the party whip attracts disqualification unless permitted or condoned by the party within 15 days.

n8e3b9a052ad.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kuldip Nayar case – Introduction of the Tenth Schedule
Thirty-third Amendment – Removal of the office-of-profit disqualification
Kihoto Hollohan case – Judicial review of decisions under the Tenth Schedule
Article 103 – Decision on defection by the President
n8e3b9a052ad.x: Kihoto Hollohan (1992) held decisions under the Tenth Schedule subject to judicial review. Kuldip Nayar concerned Rajya Sabha domicile, the 33rd Amendment resignation procedure; Article 103 does not govern defection.

n92c902a422f.s: A person elected to both Parliament and a State Legislature must resign the State seat within ____ days, failing which the Parliament seat falls vacant.
n92c902a422f.x: Under the Prohibition of Simultaneous Membership Rules, 1950, the State seat must be resigned within 14 days, otherwise the seat in Parliament becomes vacant.

nd9d37bbc083.s: The Rajya Sabha Secretariat functions under the control of the:
nd9d37bbc083.x: The parliamentary Secretariats are independent of the executive: the Rajya Sabha Secretariat is under the Chairman and the Lok Sabha Secretariat under the Speaker.

n221eef07c90.s: The readjustment of Lok Sabha constituencies on the basis of the 2001 Census was done by the Delimitation Commission headed by:
n221eef07c90.x: The 87th Amendment enabled readjustment on the 2001 Census; the work was done by the Delimitation Commission under Justice Kuldip Singh.

na8edbdf2566.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A candidate for Parliament must be a registered elector in a parliamentary constituency.
2. A Rajya Sabha candidate must be domiciled in the State from which he is elected.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
na8edbdf2566.x: A parliamentary candidate must be a registered elector in a parliamentary constituency; the domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha candidates was removed in 2003.

nindian-polity-8-25.s:
Consider the following about the veto powers of the President:
1. Absolute veto
2. Suspensive veto
3. Pocket veto
Which of the above does the President possess?
nindian-polity-8-25.x: The President has an absolute veto, a suspensive veto (returning a Bill once) and a pocket veto (keeping it pending).

nindian-polity-76-19.s: The lowest representation of women, only 19 MPs, was recorded in which Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-76-19.x: The 6th Lok Sabha (1977) had the fewest women members, only 19 MPs.

nd955df17d0e.s: Parliament in India normally holds which three sessions in a year?
nd955df17d0e.x: There is no fixed constitutional calendar, but Parliament normally has Budget, Monsoon and Winter sessions.

n25b92b8a024.s:
Arrange in the correct procedural sequence after the business of a session concludes:
1. Prorogation by the President
2. Adjournment sine die by the Speaker or Chairman
3. Reassembly in a new session
4. Recess
n25b92b8a024.x: The Speaker or Chairman first adjourns the House sine die, the President then prorogues it, a recess follows and the House reassembles in a new session.

n7af571a485c.s: A Member of Parliament enjoys freedom from arrest in civil cases during the session and:
n7af571a485c.x: The privilege covers civil arrest during the session and forty days before and after it; it does not cover criminal cases or preventive detention.

nindian-polity-8-12.s: Under Article 123, the President can promulgate an Ordinance when:
o: A National Emergency is in operation
The Rajya Sabha rejects a Bill
nindian-polity-8-12.x: The President issues Ordinances under Article 123 only when Parliament (either House) is not in session.

nindian-polity-38-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: A sitting is a daily meeting of the House during a session.
Prorogation terminates the House itself but not its session.
Dissolution ends the life of the House and applies only to the Lok Sabha.
Adjournment terminates a sitting for a specified period.
nindian-polity-38-2.x: Prorogation ends the session, not the House; only dissolution ends the House, and only the Lok Sabha can be dissolved.

nindian-polity-38-28.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Recess is the period between the prorogation of a session and the start of a new session.
2. During recess, the President may issue ordinances under Article 123.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-38-28.x: A recess is the gap between prorogation and the next session, and during it the President can issue ordinances under Article 123.

n2c162a2782c.s: A Financial Bill of category I:
o: Can be introduced in either House of Parliament
Can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha
Can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and both Houses have equal powers in its passage
Can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days
n2c162a2782c.x: A Financial Bill of category I can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, but unlike a Money Bill both Houses have equal powers in its passage.

nindian-polity-2-11.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 93 deals with the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
2. Article 108 deals with a joint sitting.
3. Article 112 deals with the Annual Financial Statement.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-polity-2-11.x: All three are correct: Article 93 – Speaker and Deputy Speaker; Article 108 – joint sitting; Article 112 – Annual Financial Statement.

nabe239e1115.s: Parliamentary privileges in India, which remain uncodified, continue under:
nabe239e1115.x: Parliamentary privileges have not been comprehensively codified; they continue under Article 105(3), historically based on those of the British House of Commons.

n0cddc1733a9.s: If the Rajya Sabha approves a National Emergency while the Lok Sabha is dissolved, the new Lok Sabha must approve it within ____ of its first sitting.
n0cddc1733a9.x: The Rajya Sabha may approve the proclamation for the time being; the newly constituted Lok Sabha must approve it within thirty days of its first sitting.

n9ccaa64610a.s: The resolution to remove Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, rejected by voice vote on 11 March 2026, was moved under:
n9ccaa64610a.x: The removal resolution against Speaker Om Birla was moved under Article 94(c) and rejected by voice vote on 11 March 2026.

n5085dcb8013.s:
Consider the following statements about the Panel of Chairpersons of the Lok Sabha:
1. It is nominated by the Speaker and may have up to ten members.
2. A member of the panel may preside when the office of Speaker is vacant.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n5085dcb8013.x: The Speaker nominates up to ten members to the panel; a panel member may preside when both Speaker and Deputy Speaker are absent, but not when the Speaker's office is vacant.

nindian-polity-57-3.s:
Consider the following statements about election as Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The person must already be an elected member of the Lok Sabha.
2. A non-member may be chosen Speaker if elected to the House within six months.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-57-3.x: The Speaker must already be an elected Lok Sabha member; the six-month relaxation applies only to Ministers.

nindian-polity-58-3.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Deputy Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members.
2. The Constitution requires the Deputy Speaker to belong to the Opposition.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-58-3.x: The Deputy Speaker is elected by the House from among its members; choosing an Opposition member is only a parliamentary convention, not a constitutional requirement.

nc32529eaeda.s:
While a resolution for his removal is under consideration, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. cannot preside over the House.
2. may vote in the first instance but not in the event of a tie.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nc32529eaeda.x: Under Article 96 the Speaker cannot preside during consideration of his removal resolution, but may speak, take part and vote in the first instance, though not cast a vote in case of a tie.

na07b41aa122.s: In January 2026, the Supreme Court upheld the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman's power under Article 91 to decide a judge-removal motion (Chairman's office vacant) in the:
na07b41aa122.x: In the Justice Varma case (January 2026), the Supreme Court upheld the Deputy Chairman's power under Article 91 to decide a judge-removal motion while the Chairman's office was vacant.

n906b367d1cf.s: As of 2026, who is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
n906b367d1cf.x: C.P. Radhakrishnan, as Vice-President, is the ex officio Chairman; Harivansh was Deputy Chairman (term ended 9 April 2026) and S. Radhakrishnan was the first Chairman (1952-62).

nindian-polity-57-31.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Speaker of the Lok Sabha – Meira Kumar
nindian-polity-57-31.x: G.V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker (1952–56); Meira Kumar was the first woman Speaker and Sumitra Mahajan the second.

nindian-polity-57-10.s:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker on dissolution of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Speaker vacates office immediately on dissolution.
2. The Speaker continues until immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Lok Sabha.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-57-10.x: The Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution; he continues until just before the new Lok Sabha first meets.

ndceb51224a5.s:
With reference to Article 98 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. Each House of Parliament has separate secretarial staff.
2. Posts common to both Houses may be created.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
ndceb51224a5.x: Article 98 gives each House its own secretarial staff while permitting the creation of posts common to both Houses.

n77f1d6ca2cb.s: The office of Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha has been vacant since:
n77f1d6ca2cb.x: The Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker post has been vacant since June 2019; the office was also reported vacant in eight State Assemblies.

n664ce45309b.s: Which of the following is considered the most effective method of day-to-day vigilance over the executive?
n664ce45309b.x: Question Hour is regarded as the most effective day-to-day check on the executive because Ministers must answer questions.

nf2348f7c728.s:
Consider the following statements about Zero Hour:
1. It is an informal Indian parliamentary innovation in use since 1962.
2. It is mentioned in the Rules of Procedure of both Houses.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nf2348f7c728.x: Zero Hour is an informal Indian innovation in use since 1962 and is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure.

n82bfaa1424b.s: In the Lok Sabha, the time immediately after Question Hour, when members raise urgent matters without prior notice, is called:
n82bfaa1424b.x: Zero Hour begins immediately after Question Hour; members raise matters with only same-day intimation to the Presiding Officer.

nbf95831bbe0.s: The Calling Attention procedure, an Indian innovation included in the Rules of Procedure, dates from:
nbf95831bbe0.x: Calling Attention is an Indian innovation dating from 1954 and is provided for in the Rules of Procedure.

nindian-polity-34-14.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Starred questions and short notice questions both permit supplementary questions.
2. Unstarred questions and short notice questions both receive written answers.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-34-14.x: Starred and short notice questions both allow supplementaries; a short notice question gets an oral answer, so only unstarred questions get written answers.

nindian-polity-34-15.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Starred questions are marked with an asterisk.
2. Unstarred questions carry no asterisk.
3. Short notice questions are identified by an asterisk.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-polity-34-15.x: Starred questions carry an asterisk and unstarred questions do not; a short notice question is marked by its shorter notice, not an asterisk.

nindian-polity-33-1.s: The primary purpose of Question Hour in Parliament is to:
o: Enforce accountability of the Council of Ministers
Discuss only matters of urgent public importance
nindian-polity-33-1.x: Question Hour and related hours exist to enforce executive accountability and control over the Council of Ministers.

n3021436b15f.s:
Consider the following statements about the Committee of Privileges:
1. In the Lok Sabha it has 10 members nominated by the Speaker.
2. In the Rajya Sabha it has 10 members nominated by the Chairman.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n3021436b15f.x: The Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges has 15 members nominated by the Speaker; the Rajya Sabha Committee has 10 members nominated by the Chairman.

ne6abb27180a.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Select Committee on a Bill consists of members of one House only.
2. A Joint Committee on a Bill consists of members of both Houses.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
ne6abb27180a.x: A Select Committee has members of one House; a Joint Committee has members of both Houses and is formed on a motion adopted in the House.

nindian-polity-39-23.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. 489 seats were contested in the first Lok Sabha general elections.
2. G.V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-39-23.x: Both are correct: 489 seats were contested in the first Lok Sabha elections and G.V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker.

nindian-polity-55-24.s: If a Confidence Motion moved by the Government is defeated in the Lok Sabha:
o: The Lok Sabha is automatically dissolved
The motion is referred to the Committee of Privileges
nindian-polity-55-24.x: Defeat of a confidence motion shows the Government has lost the Lok Sabha's support, so it falls.

nindian-polity-55-45.s:
Consider the following statements about Rule 184 of the Lok Sabha:
1. It permits a discussion on a matter of public interest followed by a formal motion and voting.
2. Defeat of a motion under Rule 184 can threaten the ruling party.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-55-45.x: Rule 184 allows a discussion ending in a formal motion and vote, and defeat on that vote can threaten the ruling party.

nindian-polity-38-32.s:
Consider the following statements about a no-confidence motion:
1. It can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
2. It requires the support of 50 members.
3. Reasons must be stated while moving it.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-polity-38-32.x: A no-confidence motion (Rule 198) is moved only in the Lok Sabha with the support of 50 members; it needs no reasons, unlike a censure motion.

nb3265088933.s:
Consider the following statements about State Legislatures:
1. They use the same devices as Parliament, such as Question Hour and motions, to control the executive.
2. They also use estimates and public accounts committees for this purpose.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nb3265088933.x: State Legislatures use the same parliamentary devices for executive control and also use estimates and public accounts committees.

na5a31ca13a9.s: Biometric attendance for MLAs in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly was introduced from the:
na5a31ca13a9.x: Andhra Pradesh introduced biometric attendance for MLAs from its Budget Session in 2026.

nindian-polity-35-7.s:
Consider the following statements about the three Financial Committees of Parliament:
1. Their members are elected by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
2. Each has a tenure of one year.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-35-7.x: Members of the PAC, Estimates and Public Undertakings Committees are elected by proportional representation by single transferable vote, for one year.

nf5f6e41c9a2.s:
Consider the following statements about the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes:
1. No minister can be a member of the Committee.
2. A minister may become a member if nominated by the Speaker.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nf5f6e41c9a2.x: No minister can be a member of the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

nindian-polity-35-10.s: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee was first constituted as an ad-hoc committee in:
nindian-polity-35-10.x: It was first set up as an ad-hoc committee on 16 May 2000 and made permanent in 2015.

nindian-polity-35-11.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee:
1. It was made a permanent committee in 2015.
2. It can take up matters that are sub-judice.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-35-11.x: The Ethics Committee became permanent in 2015, but it cannot take up matters pending in court.

ndff73d322ef.s: A half-an-hour discussion in Parliament is held on:
o: A matter of urgent public importance requiring adjournment of the House
A matter already sufficiently debated but requiring factual elucidation
ndff73d322ef.x: A half-an-hour discussion is held on a matter sufficiently debated that needs further factual elucidation; it involves no formal motion or vote.

n062dfe0a9d0.s: Which of the following pairs of cut motions is correctly matched?
o: Policy cut – Reduction of the demand by Rs 100
Economy cut – Reduction by a specified amount
Token cut – Reduction of the demand to Re 1
Policy cut – Reduction by a specified amount
n062dfe0a9d0.x: An economy cut reduces the demand by a specified amount; a policy cut reduces it to Re 1 and a token cut by Rs 100.

n57e359044f7.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: One-line Whip – Direction to attend the House
Two-line Whip – Direction to attend the House
n57e359044f7.x: A two-line Whip directs members to attend; a one-line Whip is informative and a three-line Whip gives a strict voting direction.

n08f0b1332c4.s:
Consider the following statements about a no-confidence motion:
1. Reasons for moving it must be stated.
2. The Speaker decides whether to admit it.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n08f0b1332c4.x: The Speaker has discretion to admit or reject a no-confidence motion; reasons need not be stated, and it can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.

n1c112242c03.s: The no-confidence motion carried against the Prakasam ministry of Andhra State in November 1954 was moved by:
n1c112242c03.x: Gouthu Latchanna's motion was carried by 69 votes to 68 in November 1954, and the Prakasam ministry fell.

n59b3767a915.s: A Government Bill is normally drafted by the:
o: Concerned department in association with the Law Ministry
n59b3767a915.x: A Government Bill is drafted by the concerned department with the Law Ministry; a Private Member's Bill is drafted by the member.

n2e3a9d9e946.s: The last Private Member's Bill to become law was enacted in:
n2e3a9d9e946.x: Only 14 Private Members' Bills have become law, the last in 1970.

ndba93d8da6f.s:
Consider the following statements about the President's action on a Money Bill:
1. The President may give or withhold assent to it.
2. The President may return it once to Parliament for reconsideration.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
ndba93d8da6f.x: Under Article 111 the President may assent to or withhold assent from a Money Bill but cannot return it for reconsideration.

n89eb477cfe5.s: A Money Bill can be introduced only:
o: In either House by any member with the Speaker's consent
In the Lok Sabha by a minister on the President's recommendation
In the Lok Sabha by a private member with the Rajya Sabha's approval
In the Rajya Sabha by a minister on the President's recommendation
n89eb477cfe5.x: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, only by a minister, and only on the President's recommendation.

nb5d9070a768.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The President cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration.
2. The President can return Financial Bills-I and II for reconsideration.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nb5d9070a768.x: A Money Bill cannot be returned for reconsideration, whereas Financial Bills-I and II can be.

nae9a64f6879.s:
Consider the following statements about a Financial Bill-II under Article 117(3):
1. It can be introduced in either House.
2. The President's recommendation is required at the consideration stage.
3. The Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject it.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nae9a64f6879.x: A Financial Bill-II may be introduced in either House and needs the President's recommendation at the consideration stage; the Rajya Sabha may amend or reject it.

nindian-polity-21-1.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 79, Parliament consists of the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
2. The President is a member of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-21-1.x: Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses; the President is an integral part of Parliament but not a member of either House.

nindian-polity-21-7.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
nindian-polity-21-7.x: Constitution Amendment Bills come under Article 368; ordinary Bills under Articles 107–108, Money Bills under 109–110 and Financial Bills (I) under 117(1).

n60ed084cc29.s: R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first Union Budget of independent India on:
n60ed084cc29.x: R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first Union Budget of independent India on 26 November 1947.

nindian-polity-61-32.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Article 112 – Annual Financial Statement
2. Article 115 – Vote on account and vote of credit
3. Article 114 – Appropriation Bills
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
nindian-polity-61-32.x: Article 112 covers the Annual Financial Statement and Article 114 the Appropriation Bill; Article 115 deals with supplementary, additional and excess grants, while vote on account and vote of credit fall under Article 116.

ne5d39781d7f.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The CAG audits the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account of the Union.
2. The CAG audits the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account of the States.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
ne5d39781d7f.x: The Comptroller and Auditor General audits all three funds of both the Union and the States.

nindian-polity-61-7.s:
Consider the following statements about charged expenditure:
1. It is not submitted to the vote of Parliament.
2. It cannot be discussed by either House of Parliament.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-61-7.x: Charged expenditure is not put to vote, but both Houses can discuss it.

nindian-polity-79-13.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The salaries of Supreme Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. The salaries of High Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
3. The pensions of High Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-polity-79-13.x: Supreme Court judges' salaries and High Court judges' pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; High Court judges' salaries come from the State's fund.

nindian-polity-79-19.s: The Third Schedule of the Constitution deals with:
o: Emoluments, allowances and privileges of office-holders
nindian-polity-79-19.x: The Third Schedule contains the forms of oaths and affirmations; emoluments, allowances and privileges are in the Second Schedule.

nindian-polity-61-17.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Salaries and administrative expenses of the Election Commission are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. Salaries and allowances of the Prime Minister and Union Ministers are votable expenditure.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-61-17.x: The Election Commission's salaries and running costs are voted, not charged; the salaries of the Prime Minister and Ministers are also voted.

nindian-polity-79-16.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
nindian-polity-79-16.x: Ministers' salaries fall under Article 75(6); the President's under 59(3), Supreme Court judges' under 125 and the CAG's under 148(3).

nindian-polity-79-30.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Election Commission's expenditure is votable.
2. The salaries of the Prime Minister and Ministers are voted through annual Demands for Grants.
3. The Vice-President receives a separate salary as Vice-President.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-polity-79-30.x: The Election Commission's expenditure and Ministers' salaries are voted; the Vice-President is paid only as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

nindian-polity-38-66.s:
Consider the following statements about an Appropriation Bill:
1. It authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. It covers voted grants and charged expenditure.
3. It is an advance grant for part of a financial year.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-polity-38-66.x: The Appropriation Bill permits withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund for voted grants and charged expenditure; an advance grant for part of the year is a vote on account.

n3980ddf3cec.s: The Economic Stabilisation Fund proposed in the Union Budget 2026-27 has a proposed size of:
n3980ddf3cec.x: The proposed Economic Stabilisation Fund is Rs 1 lakh crore; Rs 30,000 crore is the corpus of the Contingency Fund of India.

nab202dba8b4.s: Which of the following is an ad hoc committee of Parliament?
nab202dba8b4.x: Ad hoc committees are of two kinds: inquiry committees on a particular subject, and Select or Joint Committees constituted to examine Bills.

ned084736c7a.s: A Bill is referred to a Select Committee or a Joint Committee by:
o: A recommendation of the Business Advisory Committee
A decision of the Union Cabinet
ned084736c7a.x: Referral of a Bill to a Select or Joint Committee takes place through a motion in the House.

n3854722eb1a.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the parliamentary 'watchdog' group of committees?
n3854722eb1a.x: The watchdog group comprises the Committees on Subordinate Legislation and Government Assurances, the Estimates Committee, PAC, COPU and DRSCs; the Business Advisory Committee only allots time for business.

nindian-polity-35-3.s: How many Department-Related Standing Committees are there in Parliament?
nindian-polity-35-3.x: There are 24 DRSCs: 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha. 22 is the strength of the PAC.

n83d07353b4c.s:
Consider the following statements about the Committee of Privileges:
1. The Lok Sabha committee has 15 members nominated by the Speaker.
2. The Rajya Sabha committee has 15 members.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n83d07353b4c.x: The Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges has 15 members nominated by the Speaker; the Rajya Sabha committee has 10.

n250eee6fdfd.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Public Accounts Committee – 1950, on John Mathai's recommendation
Committee on Public Undertakings – 1964, on the Krishna Menon Committee's recommendation
Departmentally Related Standing Committees – 1921, under the Government of India Act, 1919
Estimates Committee (present form) – 1993, on the Rules Committee's recommendation
n250eee6fdfd.x: COPU was set up in 1964 on the Krishna Menon Committee's recommendation; the PAC dates from 1921, the Estimates Committee's present form from 1950 (John Mathai) and DRSCs from 1993 (Rules Committee).

n2f05595ebe9.s: The Public Accounts Committee primarily examines:
o: Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and CAG audit reports
n2f05595ebe9.x: The PAC examines the Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor-General.

n95be8cec87d.s: The Public Accounts Committee checks whether government expenditure remained within the scope of the:
o: Demand for grant approved by Parliament
n95be8cec87d.x: The PAC checks whether money was spent within the scope of the demand for grant approved by Parliament.

naf46605db41.s:
Departmentally Related Standing Committees scrutinise:
1. Demands for grants
2. Bills referred to them
3. Annual reports of ministries
Which of the above are correct?
naf46605db41.x: DRSCs scrutinise demands for grants, referred Bills, annual reports and long-term policy of the ministries under them.

n1d1f88012b4.s:
Assertion (A): The chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is generally selected from the Opposition.
Reason (R): Selection of an Opposition member as PAC chairperson is a constitutional rule.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n1d1f88012b4.x: Since 1967 the PAC chairman has been an Opposition member, but this is a convention, not a constitutional or statutory rule.

nindian-polity-35-1.s: Parliamentary committees mainly help Parliament control the administration by:
o: Framing the daily agenda of the House
Undertaking detailed scrutiny that the whole House has no time for
nindian-polity-35-1.x: Committees are a main instrument of parliamentary control, doing the detailed, complex scrutiny the whole House cannot.

nc3d9469343f.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 105 – Courts not to inquire into proceedings of Parliament
nc3d9469343f.x: Article 194 deals with State Legislature privileges; Article 105 with Parliament's privileges, Article 122 with parliamentary proceedings and Article 212 with State Legislature proceedings.

n5e0a45f8f8d.s: The principal objective of the anti-defection law is to:
o: Ensure internal democracy within political parties
Curb defections for office and promote stable governments
Limit the size of the Council of Ministers
n5e0a45f8f8d.x: The law was meant to curb horse-trading and defections for office, promoting party discipline and stable governments.

n484d06eedf6.s: The 1984 defection led by Nadendla Bhaskara Rao toppled the Andhra Pradesh government of:
n484d06eedf6.x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao's defection toppled N.T. Rama Rao's government in 1984; NTR was restored after a month, strengthening the demand for the 1985 law.

nindian-polity-77-5.s: Jammu & Kashmir enacted its own State anti-defection law in:
nindian-polity-77-5.x: Jammu and Kashmir passed its own anti-defection law in 1979, before the national law of 1985.

nindian-polity-77-6.s:
Consider the following statements about the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:
1. It strengthened the anti-defection law.
2. It deleted the one-third split exception.
3. It capped the Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lower House.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-polity-77-6.x: All three are correct: the 91st Amendment strengthened the anti-defection law, removed the one-third split and capped the ministry at 15%.

nindian-polity-77-11.s:
Under the anti-defection law, a member is protected from disqualification when:
1. Prior permission of the party was obtained.
2. The party condones the vote against the whip within 15 days.
3. At least two-thirds of the legislature party agrees to a merger.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-polity-77-11.x: A member is protected with prior permission, if the party condones the vote within 15 days, or in a merger backed by two-thirds of the legislature party.

nindian-polity-77-23.s:
Consider the following statements about an independent elected member:
1. He is disqualified on joining any political party after election.
2. He may become a Minister without taking party membership.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-77-23.x: An independent member is disqualified only on joining a party after election; becoming a Minister without joining a party does not disqualify him.

nindian-polity-77-17.s:
Consider the following statements about the anti-defection law:
1. The one-third split exception continues under the present law.
2. A merger is protected when at least two-thirds of the legislature party agrees to it.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-77-17.x: The one-third split exception was abolished in 2003; a merger backed by two-thirds of the legislature party is protected.

n0c3b794ab23.s: Which of the following is a newer proposal concerning the anti-defection law?
o: Exempting independent members from the law
Fixed timelines for Speakers and an independent tribunal
n0c3b794ab23.x: Newer proposals include fixed constitutional timelines for Speakers and an independent tribunal, the latter suggested for consideration by the Supreme Court in 2020.

n643cf6afb57.s: In the Telangana Speaker matter, how much time did the Supreme Court later allow for deciding the last two of ten BRS disqualification petitions?
n643cf6afb57.x: After a time-bound direction, the Supreme Court gave three weeks for the last two of ten BRS petitions, warning of contempt.

n5301ea4de2d.s: In the 'resignation route' used to avoid disqualification proceedings, legislators:
o: Seek prior permission from the Election Commission before switching parties
Abstain from every vote until the next election
Resign, lowering the majority mark, and later re-contest on the new party's ticket
Merge into the new party without resigning
n5301ea4de2d.x: In the resignation route, MLAs resign instead of defecting, reducing the majority mark without disqualification, and may re-contest on the new party's ticket.

n09f787e59a7.s: Delay by Speakers in deciding disqualification petitions is a concern mainly because:
o: Speakers need the Governor's approval to decide
The Election Commission must concur in every decision
Petitions must first be heard by the High Court
There is no fixed time limit and Speakers remain members of their parties
n09f787e59a7.x: There is no fixed time limit, and Speakers, who do not resign from their parties, decide petitions in a partisan context.

nb14c435f09d.s: In April 2026, seven Rajya Sabha MPs of which party joined the BJP, an episode cited as misuse of the merger exception?
nb14c435f09d.x: Seven AAP Rajya Sabha MPs joined the BJP in April 2026; twenty TMC MPs joining the NPCI in June 2026 was the other example cited.

n4a77ead8527.s: The disqualification petitions against 23 YSRCP MLAs who moved to the TDP between 2014 and 2019 were:
o: Decided by the Supreme Court in 2014
Upheld, and the MLAs disqualified immediately
n4a77ead8527.x: The petitions were never decided, a standard example of delay by the Speaker in anti-defection proceedings.

nindian-polity-77-15.s: The time limit prescribed in the Tenth Schedule for the Presiding Officer to decide a defection petition is:
nindian-polity-77-15.x: The Tenth Schedule sets no time limit for deciding a defection petition, which is often criticised.

nbfc727964d6.s: The two-thirds rule under Paragraph 4 of the Tenth Schedule has been criticised because it may be used to:
o: Protect individual dissent against the whip
nbfc727964d6.x: The Paragraph 4 two-thirds rule has been used as a defence for mass defection and so attracts criticism.

nb6a26bdbc8c.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In India, less than one-fifth of Bills are referred to committees.
2. In the United Kingdom, every Bill is examined by committees of both Houses.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nb6a26bdbc8c.x: Less than one-fifth of Indian Bills go to committees, while every UK Bill is examined by committees of both Houses.
